# The third spelling of one settlement: the split named outright.
#
# Same physical move as `second_usd_invoice_takes_the_parked_credit.txt` — the
# customer's parked 100.00 USD settles this invoice — but reached by naming the
# split rather than letting the transaction be searched. A guid says *which*
# split, not where it came from, so this spends the credit exactly as the
# shorter spelling does and gets the same accounting.
#
# This is the route the ambiguity refusal sends readers down by name, so it is
# the one a transaction carrying two of an owner's credits has to be settled
# through.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_foreign_currency_cost_basis.py.

invoice "INV-USD-NAMED"
	customer_id: "C-US"
	currency: USD
	date_opened: 2026-03-01
	entry:
		date: 2026-03-01
		description: "More consulting"
		action: "Hours"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
	posted:
		date: 2026-03-01
		due: 2026-04-01
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
		memo: "Invoice INV-USD-NAMED"
		accumulate: true
	payment:
		date: 2026-03-01
		amount: 100
		bank_account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
		txn_guid: "TXN_GUID"
		txn_split_guid: "SPLIT_GUID"
		memo: "Settled from the credit on account"
